question: Coal deposits in the North-Eastern Plateau are primarily linked to which river valley?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Damodar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Damodar River Valley**, located in the eastern region of India, is historically known as the "Ruhr of India" due to its rich **coal deposits**.
 
• The North-Eastern Plateau region, which spans across **Jharkhand and West Bengal**, is home to the largest coal reserves in India. It is primarily linked to the Damodar River.
 
• Major coalfields such as **Jharia, Raniganj, Bokaro, and Giridih** are situated along the Damodar River Valley, making it a vital area for India’s coal production.
 
• The Damodar River plays a crucial role in shaping the geography and geology of this region, contributing to the formation of coal deposits over millions of years. *Hence, this answer is correct.*
 
• The coal in this region is primarily used for **power generation**, steel production, and other industrial purposes. Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC) is a significant stakeholder in utilizing these resources.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Coal Deposits in India:**

 
 
• India has the **fifth-largest coal reserves** in the world, with major deposits concentrated in regions such as the **North-Eastern Plateau**, **Central India**, and **Southern India**.
 
• The Damodar Valley coalfields are part of the **Gondwana coal belt**, which dates back over 250 million years.
 
• Coal is the backbone of India’s energy sector, contributing over **50% of the energy mix**.
 
 
 
• **Features of the Damodar River:**
 
 
• The Damodar River originates from the **Chota Nagpur Plateau** in Jharkhand and flows through West Bengal before joining the Hooghly River.
 
• It is approximately **592 kilometers** long and is known for its fertile valley and industrial significance.
 
• The river is prone to flooding, earning it the nickname "Sorrow of Bengal" historically. However, the creation of **Dams and Barrages** under the Damodar Valley Corporation has helped mitigate this.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Coal:**
 
 
• **Thermal Power Generation:** Coal is the primary fuel for thermal power plants, contributing significantly to India’s electricity production.
 
• **Steel Industry:** Coking coal from regions like Jharia is crucial for steel production in industries such as **Tata Steel**.
 
• **Industrial Use:** Coal is used in cement manufacturing, chemical industries, and other industrial applications.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Coalfields in India:**

 
 
• **Jharia Coalfield:** Located in Jharkhand, known for high-quality coking coal.
 
• **Raniganj Coalfield:** Located in West Bengal, known for non-coking coal used in power plants.
 
• **Bokaro Coalfield:** Also in Jharkhand, contributing to industrial coal production.
 
• **Talcher Coalfield:** Located in Odisha, a major contributor to thermal coal output.
 
 
 
• **Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC):**
 
 
• Established in **1948**, DVC is responsible for irrigation, flood control, and power generation in the Damodar Valley region.
 
• It operates **thermal power stations** and manages coal resources efficiently.
